application_sentences: The QUV/uvc model uses UVC lamps to deliver light concentrated at 254 nm to test for material durability against photodegradation effects resulting from exposure to UVC light.

The new Q-SUN “E” model xenon test chambers allow users to test at higher irradiance and/or longer lamp lifetimes - up to 3000 hours at standard irradiances and 1000 hours at high irradiances - through the use of new “plus” lamps.
The chamber’s direct water spray feature can be used for testing samples to thermal shock and the resulting mechanical erosion.

Two lamp types are available, selected based on the intended application: UVA-340 lamps closely replicate the short-wave UV portion of natural sunlight and are used for most outdoor material testing, while UVB-313 lamps provide a more aggressive spectrum for accelerated screening.

ASTM G154 does not itself define acceptance criteria or specify exposure conditions for particular applications; results are best used for comparative ranking or compliance with specified exposure requirements.

Surface and volume resistivity analyses conducted at cryogenic and elevated temperatures (up to 250°C) are also available, as well as other electrical tests for plastic materials, including those conducted according to ASTM standards.

No direct correlation exists between accelerated exposure duration and outdoor service life; results are best used for comparative ranking of materials or compliance with specified exposure requirements.
Specimen size: Typically, flat plaques or disks are used for accelerated weathering studies.

Can ASTM G154 be used to test metals? ASTM G154 is often not utilized for metals because it is intended for nonmetallic materials such as plastics and coatings.
